title: The objective approach and its critics
shortTitle: The objective approach and its critics
summary: The introductory quotations disagree about the place of actual intention.
notes: Hand’s formulation emphasizes what words ordinarily signify; Frank’s response resists excluding actual shared intent. Lucy, Keller, and Leonard then vary the evidence of serious commitment. The notes also ask what discovery and jury fact-finding can establish and how intentions are attributed to organizational parties. These are interpretive and evidentiary questions rather than a command to ignore every mental fact.
